{{Short description|American physicist}}
'''Andreas J. Albrecht''' is a [[theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]] and [[cosmologist]] who is a professor and chair of the physics department at the [[University of California, Davis]].<ref name="CV">[http://physics.ucdavis.edu/Cosmology/albrecht/Myinfo/CV.pdf CV] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110824105706/http://physics.ucdavis.edu/Cosmology/albrecht/Myinfo/CV.pdf |date=August 24, 2011 }} of Dr Andreas Albrecht.</ref> He is one of the founders of [[inflation theory|inflationary cosmology]]<ref>A. Albrecht and P. Steinhardt, ''Cosmology for Grand Unified Theories with Radiatively Induced Symmetry Breaking'', Phys. Rev. Lett.  48, 1220 (1982).</ref> and studies the formation of the early universe, cosmic structure, and [[dark energy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://albrecht.ucdavis.edu/Myinfo/Research%20Interests.pdf |author=Andreas Albrecht |title=Research Interests of Andreas Albrecht |access-date=Feb 12, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121202024709/http://albrecht.ucdavis.edu/Myinfo/Research%20Interests.pdf |archive-date=2012-12-02 }}</ref>

==Life and career==
Albrecht graduated in 1979 from [[Cornell University]] and was awarded a doctorate in 1983 at [[University of Pennsylvania]], [[Philadelphia]] on cosmology. His thesis advisor was [[Paul Steinhardt]].

He later carried out post-doctoral research at [[University of Texas]], [[Austin, Texas|Austin]] and at [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]]. Albrecht later worked at [[Fermilab]] from 1987 to 1992 and subsequently taught at [[Imperial College]], [[London]] from 1992 to 1998.

Albrecht is a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] and [[Fellow of the Institute of Physics]] (UK).<ref name="CV" />

==Work==
Together with his thesis advisor, Albrecht developed New Inflation, solving the bubble collision problem of [[Alan Guth]]'s original model of inflation. Later, Albrecht studied the observable effects of cosmic [[topological defect]]s, contributing to ruling out [[cosmic strings]] as the dominant mechanism for structure formation.{{Citation needed|date=July 2025}}

Along with [[João Magueijo]], Albrecht independently proposed a model of [[Variable speed of light#The varying speed of light cosmology|varying speed of light cosmology]]<ref>{{cite journal |title=A time varying speed of light as a solution to cosmological puzzles |author=A. Albrecht |author2=J. Magueijo |journal=Phys. Rev. |volume=D59 |article-number=043516 |date=1999 |issue=4 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.59.043516 |arxiv=astro-ph/9811018 |bibcode=1999PhRvD..59d3516A|s2cid=56138144 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |title=Faster Than the Speed of Light: The Story of a Scientific Speculation |author=J. Magueijo |publisher=Perseus Books Group |location=Massachusetts |date=2003 |isbn=0-7382-0525-7 |url-access=registration |url=https://archive.org/details/fasterthanspeedo00magu }}</ref> which posits that the speed of light in the early universe was a trillion times faster in order to explain the [[horizon problem]] of [[physical cosmology|cosmology]].

In the 21st century, Albrecht worked on [[quantum mechanics]], as well as [[probability]] and quantum theory.<ref>{{cite news |author=Jacob Aron |url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/mg21728984.100-humble-coin-toss-thrust-to-heart-of-multiverse-debate.html |journal=New Scientist |title=Humble coin toss thrust to heart of multiverse debate |issue=2898 |date=Jan 2, 2013}}</ref>
